We have applied 29646 to target, got three possible precursors (list of three). The result from apply_template gave a tuple of three strings? Actually result: "(('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)[C@H]1C)CO',))"

So three possible outcomes: first with silyl group on side chain? Actually first has CO[Si]... second is without silyl? third is with silyl on OH.

We need to follow template order: after 29646, we need to apply 1914389 to one of the products. Which product matches? We checked matching: the third product (with silyl on OH) matched 1914389. Indeed we checked that and got True. So we should choose that as the next node.

Thus route: target -> reaction 29646 -> precursor A (choose third). Then apply 1914389 to that precursor to get its precursors.

We applied 1914389 to that third product and got result: "(('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C', 'CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC'),)". So two precursors: one is a silyl-protected molecule with a carbonyl (CC=O) inside ring; the other is an ester? Actually second is "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC". That seems like a separate fragment maybe from cleavage.

So we need to produce a linear route: target -> after 29646 -> after 1914389 -> after 1914390 -> after 149040 -> after 1914391 -> final precursors (starting materials). So each step must be applicable.

Thus we need to find a path where each template can be applied sequentially. We have some flexibility to choose which precursor from each step to continue.
